# Steve Eisman Reveals His Personal Portfolio: Every Position Explained

First listed: 2026-07-01 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [Substack: Steve Eisman Reveals His Personal Portfolio: Every Position Explained](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/steve-eisman-reveals-his-personal) - 2026-07-01

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Eisman explains his concentrated long portfolio through AI suppliers, electricity infrastructure, low-valued turnarounds, established franchises and speculative cannabis. He sells capital-intensive platforms while monitoring AI financing and power bottlenecks. NVIDIA growth and the infrastructure backlog support current demand, but most valuation and recovery theses remain undated or conditional. Charter and Meritage still face operating pressure. Apple already had its own models, Microsoft had raised debt since its IPO, and Progressive did not invent direct insurance. Glass House upside rests on unproven market access, prices and margins; scenario arithmetic is separated from investable outcomes.

A useful statement of holdings, catalysts and falsifiers, with several factual errors in supporting premises. The central multi-year and conditional investment theses should not be graded as completed returns. Capital-intensity rotation has evidence, while stock-specific valuation claims lack point-in-time consensus reconstruction. Cannabis rescheduling is real but narrower than an automatic opening of every market.

<a id="substack-203129377-c008"></a>
### 008. Technology and technology-like index members amount to roughly half the S&P 500, making his seven technology-related holdings comparable exposure.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | investment thesis | major

[Source at 5:42-6:21](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/steve-eisman-reveals-his-personal) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Position counts cannot establish capital exposure; the precise index weights are unverified.

Conditional reasoning: Seven of sixteen names is a count fraction of 43.75%. Portfolio weight instead equals their market value divided by total portfolio value. Without sizes these fractions need not agree; comparison to a capitalization-weighted index is insufficient.

Assessment test: Compare market-value weights using the same sector definition.

## Framework and tools

- Write the initial thesis and sell when it fails rather than rationalizing thesis creep.
- Distinguish growth stories from fundamentals and recognize uncertainty at regime changes.
- Separate AI suppliers from buyers bearing the capital-spending burden.
- Use cash flow, buybacks, book value, ROE and backlog to identify catalysts.
- Model speculative outcomes with explicit margins and dilution rather than a single target.
- State concrete evidence that would reduce portfolio risk.
